title: Customer Health KPI Signalbook — latency, uptime, cost/token, cache-hit
summary: Working reference for QBR cadence: precise metric definitions, measurement windows, canonical formulas, example KPI tables for customer health checks and renewal signals. Emphasis on latency distributions, uptime SLI, cost-per-token breakouts, and cache hit semantics used by Product/Eng instrumentation.
audience: CS AEs, CSMs, Solutions Eng, Eng Reliability owners
purpose: Make every QBR-friendly dashboard and renewal conversation use the same definitions and trigger thresholds. Reduce ambiguity between observed symptoms (slowness, cost spikes, cache misses) and remediation playbooks.
notes_to_self: This is a living doc — keep examples small. Add customer-specific baseline rows per account in the renewal tracker sheet. Coordinate with eng-metrics before finalizing p95 computations.
definitions: Latency (observed): time from request ingestion to first-byte sent to client for generation calls; includes routing + model inference + serialization. Measured at edge by gateway logs.
Latency p50/p95/p99: percentile latency computed on successful responses only (exclude 5xx and client-cancelled). Use sliding 7d window for short-term SLA and 30d for trend analysis.
Tail latency: p95 and p99 used as primary tail indicators. We report both 'first-byte' and 'completion' latencies when streaming is used.
Uptime (SLI): proportion of requests that receive a successful 2xx response within configured latency SLO. Default SLO for hosted tier = 99.95% over 30d. Downtime = 1 - SLI.

Cost per token: total service cost allocated to a customer divided by tokens billed over the same period. Includes model compute, memory overhead, and proportional infra (not including unrelated platform costs). Calculated weekly and monthly.

Cache hit rate: fraction of requests where prefix/KV/persistent cache avoided full model inference. Measured as hits / (hits + misses) at the inference routing layer. Important: classify partial hits (KV partial) as misses for conservative accounting unless stated otherwise.

Warm vs cold starts: 'cold' denotes model shard or instance boot where latency is materially higher — flag cold-started requests and exclude from steady-state SLO assessment for first 10 minutes after scale-up events.
Error budget: monthly allowance derived from uptime SLO; used to prioritize remediation and customer communications prior to renewals. Example: 99.95% monthly SLO -> ~21.6 minutes allowed downtime.

Measurement boundaries: metrics should be sourced from the same pipeline (gateway + inference telemetry) to avoid mismatch between token counts and request latencies. Cross-check sample raw logs when building a new dashboard.

Attribution note: cost/token should be shown both 'gross' (platform-billed) and 'net' (after discounts/reservations) for renewal economics conversations. Use gross for internal ops, net for billing-sensitive customers.

Alerting prevalence: treat sustained p95 increase > 2x baseline for 6 hours as a high-priority incident. For cost spikes, >30% week-over-week increase without traffic growth -> investigate caching, model changes, or quantization regressions.
Data integrity: if token telemetry < 98% of expected (gateway vs billing), mark data as 'partial' and avoid locking KPIs for that window. TODO: add automated flag in sheet.
Sample windows: immediate (last 24h), short-term (7d rolling), trend (30d rolling), contract review (90d).
formulas_and_examples: Latency percentiles: compute on request-level latencies (ms). For p95: sort latencies ascending, pick value at position ceil(0.95 * N). Use interpolation for small N.
Uptime SLI formula: SLI = (#requests_with_2xx_and_latency<=SLO) / (total_requests_considered). Exclude scheduled maintenance windows with pre-approved tickets.
Cost per token (gross): total_compute_cost + infra_overhead + network_costs_assigned_to_account / tokens_billed_in_period.
Cache hit rate formula: cache_hits / (cache_hits + cache_misses). Example: 18k hits, 82k misses -> 18% hit rate.
Sample KPI snapshot (30d rolling): p50=120ms, p95=540ms, uptime=99.92%, cost_perk=0.00034 USD/token, cache_hit=0.21.
Renewal trigger example: if 30d p95 > SLA_p95_threshold OR uptime < 99.9% for two consecutive 30d windows -> flag for renewal risk discussion and prioritized eng investigation.
Normalization: when comparing cost/token across customers, normalize for average sequence length and streaming vs batch differences. Report both raw cost/token and length-normalized cost/token.
kpi_table_rows: Acme Corp | 95 | 420 | 99.88 | 0.00040 | 18 | moderate (p95 slightly above baseline)
Brightlane | 160 | 760 | 99.70 | 0.00029 | 45 | high (cache hit high but uptime degradation)
playbook_snippets: If p95 rises >2x baseline: 1) open 'latency-incident' ticket, 2) collect sample traces (10 requests across p50/p95/p99), 3) check recent rollouts/model changes, 4) if cache hit drops, consider cache warm-up script.
If cache hit rate falls by >20 percentage points week-over-week: run cache bloom-check, validate prefix keys, confirm client SDK version and prompt canonicalization.
If cost/token rises without traffic growth: re-evaluate model variant (quantized vs fp16) and batching config; run Redwood Optimize report for suggested batch size and KV cache settings.
Uptime drift action: for sustained 30d uptime < SLO, escalate to eng-sre, propose reserved capacity or traffic shaping for critical routes during renewal conversations.

Customer conversation template (AE/CS): start with baseline snapshot, explain delta drivers (traffic, prompts, model), share concrete remediation plan and expected impact on KPIs (e.g., "warm cache + 30% fewer calls -> p95 down 200ms -> cost -15%" ).
